tasks.task: Build the ideal customer profile from won and lost deals

items.when: Before choosing accounts, or when sales and marketing disagree on the best customers
When you have closed deals, to see loss stages, common objections and deal traits
When the profile is drafted, to test it against why deals were really won

tasks.task: Build a target account list in three tiers

items.when: When you have won and lost deals and a candidate list to score on fit and intent
When the candidate list is thin, to find more accounts with the reason each fits
When you want a second scoring of each account on fit and activity, with reasons
When account records lack size, sector or contacts and cannot be scored
When the list needs emails, roles and company details added from many sources

tasks.task: Plan the plays for each account tier

items.when: When tiers are agreed and each needs its plays, owners and budget
Two weeks before the quarter, to run the cycle from list refresh to review
When a play needs one brief with goal, audience, messages and a weekly calendar
When the plan jumps to tactics before the target and the goal are chosen

tasks.task: Write messages for each role in the buying group

items.when: When you need the pain, proof and ask for each person who uses, pays or can block
Before writing, to map what starts the search and what proof each buyer needs
When the deal is complex, to name the buyer roles and the risks around each
When a message is drafted, to face the toughest objection that role would raise
When a line sounds like any vendor, to test it and get a specific rewrite

tasks.task: Plan a one-to-one play for a top account

items.when: When one account matters enough for its own plan of people, goals and next steps
When you need the email, call script and LinkedIn message built from real signals
When the top account is already a customer, to see what else they could buy

tasks.task: Brief a LinkedIn campaign for target accounts

items.when: When the target list is agreed and tier 2 or 3 accounts need a LinkedIn campaign
When you want several hooks and formats per buying role before picking
When the campaign has run, to check audiences, lead forms, creative, bids and budgets

tasks.task: Write an outbound sequence with sales and check consent

items.when: Before any cold email or LinkedIn sequence, to check the rules in each country
When sales needs a multi-step sequence with timing and personal touches
When you must decide who to target, which signals to watch and which channels to mix
When each step needs subject lines in several angles to test
Before sending, to test each claim against the prospect's own page
When the message is long and should show one business result to a busy buyer

tasks.task: Set lead scoring and the handoff to sales

items.when: When you have won and lost leads and need fit points, engagement points and a handoff
When stages and handoff rules between marketing and sales are not written down
When you want to test the rule on real leads and see who it ranks first
When new leads sit unowned, to decide who gets each and write the handoff note

tasks.task: Reply to enquiries and follow up fast

items.when: When a batch of leads arrives, to rank them by fit and urgency with talking points
When each enquiry needs a qualified reply with real meeting times
When a lead went quiet after the first reply and needs a few polite nudges
Before a reply goes, to cut it to one clear ask

tasks.task: Plan a webinar with outline and run sheet

items.when: When a webinar is agreed, to plan it backwards from the one next step for attendees
Six weeks out, to run the countdown from topic to follow-up
When the session must teach one clear result and needs an outline and slide brief
When you need the plan to promote it across channels and partners
When the talk rambles and needs one story and one request

tasks.task: Write the registration page and invitation sequence

items.when: When the date and next step are set and invitations and reminders need writing
When the registration page needs writing for one action
When each invitation needs subject lines in several angles
When speakers and staff need posts to share the registration link
When an invitation is drafted, to get cuts and a ship or fix verdict

tasks.task: Follow up attendees, no-shows and engaged accounts

items.when: Right after the event, when you have attendee lists, poll answers and questions
When follow-ups should be grouped by what each person asked for, with promises tracked
When the recording should become posts, emails and clips for those who missed it
When the follow-up needs different subject lines for attendees and no-shows
Before the follow-up goes, to cut it to one next step

tasks.task: Plan a trade show or field event for pipeline

items.when: When an event must fill seats and turn attendees into pipeline
Before paying for a stand, to set the test, its cost and the rule for going again
Before emailing badge scans or a list from the organiser

tasks.task: Write an event recap and results report

items.when: When you have the numbers and need trends, drop-offs and next steps in one report
When you must show cost per qualified lead, not cost per registration
When the team needs one page on what to repeat and what to change next time

tasks.task: Plan a gated offer and its landing page

items.when: When there is no offer yet, to compare ideas and pick the one worth an email address
When buyers have a costly problem and useful information should start the talk
When buyers are slow and careful, to plan what earns their trust first
When the offer is chosen and its page needs writing
When the page is drafted, to rank what would stop a visitor filling the form

tasks.task: Write a nurture sequence for leads not ready to buy

items.when: When stalled leads should get useful information first, then a follow-up
When you need the full sequence with timing, subject lines and emails
When each email needs several subject lines to choose from
When the sequence has numbers, to see which emails to keep and which to fix

tasks.task: Run the monthly pipeline review with sales

items.when: First Monday of the month, with the marketing and sales leaders
When you need coverage, ageing and conversion stage by stage
When the pipeline should be watched weekly between the monthly reviews
When marketing and sales reports show different numbers for the same thing

tasks.task: Write the monthly ABM progress report

items.when: Monthly, from CRM and ad exports, for marketing and sales leaders
When nobody agrees what to track, to set short-term and long-term measures
When leaders want one page with the answer first and the decision needed

tasks.task: Split the budget and choose how to credit channels

items.when: When reports conflict, to pick a model and a way to settle them
When a new budget is proposed, to forecast low and high cases by channel
When all spend goes to lead capture and the brand share needs deciding
When the budget is set per quarter and must follow the account tiers
When a dashboard claims credit, to ask what the numbers mean and who benefits

tasks.task: Give sales the proof and collateral for target accounts

items.when: When a rival shows up in most deals and sales needs comparisons and replies
When a play needs a one-pager, objection sheet or demo script
When a customer agreed to talk and you need a case outline and approval list
When collateral is drafted, to check it speaks to each role in the buying group

tasks.task: Plan a joint campaign with a partner

items.when: When a partner serves the same accounts and a joint campaign could reach them
When both sides need a shared message brief, drafts and an approval tracker

always.when: When a message or report states a number or customer result you cannot trace
Before any email, post or page goes out, to fix lines that sound machine-written

helpers.when: When the LinkedIn campaign needs building, bidding and weekly changes in the account
When a play needs daily calls and personal outreach to named contacts
When scoring, routing or reports need building in the CRM
When an in-person event needs a venue, suppliers and a run sheet
When a play needs a report, guide or article written as the offer
When channel credit or budget questions need the data pulled and tested

gaps: No library item builds an ABM plan: tiers, plays per tier and budget per account; only the kit skill does
No library item maps a buying group and writes a message per role, or offers different angles per role
No library item works back from a revenue target to pipeline, opportunities and leads needed
No library item writes a webinar run sheet or host script, or checks a webinar outline before the day
No library item writes an event recap that ties attendees to accounts and pipeline
No library item plans a small executive dinner or roundtable for top accounts
No library item reads intent signals or website visits by account and says who to contact now
No library item checks B2B cold outreach rules by country; only the kit prompt does
No library item writes a gated report or white paper for B2B buyers
No library item sets a service agreement between marketing and sales with response times and feedback
